content: National Influenza Centers (NICs) are institutions officially recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO) for their role in influenza surveillance and research. The WHO Global Influenza Surveillance Network was established in 1952. This network consists of four WHO Collaborating Centres (WHO CCs) and 112 institutions across 83 countries, all of which are recognized by WHO as National Influenza Centers (NICs). These NICs are responsible for collecting clinical specimens within their respective countries. They perform primary virus isolation and conduct preliminary antigenic characterization of influenza viruses. Newly isolated virus strains are then sent to WHO Collaborating Centres for advanced antigenic and genetic analysis. The results of these analyses are critical in forming the basis for WHO's annual recommendations on the composition of influenza vaccines for both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Among the more than 110 National Influenza Centers, WHO Collaborating Centres and reference laboratories play a key role in the annual process of determining influenza vaccine composition recommendations.
